claims.statement: Global renewable power capacity reached 4,448 GW in 2024 after a 585 GW annual increase.
Renewables accounted for 92.5% of total power capacity expansion in 2024, with annual growth at 15.1%.
The 2030 tripling benchmark still points to 11,000 GW of renewable capacity.
Current government ambitions still sit closer to 8,000 GW by 2030.
Solar PV is on course to deliver about two-thirds of the year's increase in global renewable capacity.
Tripling renewable capacity by 2030 would cut unabated coal-fired generation by half between 2022 and 2030.

data.impact_text: cut unabated coal-fired generation by half between 2022 and 2030

claims.statement: Long permitting waits, grid investment gaps, and high financing costs still slow deployment.
World solar rose from 1,054 TWh in 2021 to 1,664 TWh in 2023, while world wind rose from 1,857 TWh to 2,319 TWh.
The bundled China 2023 row reports 584 TWh of solar generation and 886 TWh of wind generation.
